title: High-Nuclearity Lanthanide-Containing Clusters as Potential Molecular Magnetic Coolers
claim: For high-nuclearity Gd(III)-exclusive clusters, gravimetric magnetocaloric effect, reported as −ΔSM, generally increases with unpaired-electron density, so small, light ligands and a high metal/ligand mass ratio are preferred over heavier ligands or large anions.
explanation: Figure 8 plots gravimetric −ΔSM against unpaired-electron density at ΔH = 70 kOe. Acetate-supported Gd104 is given the highest spin density in that comparison and −ΔSM = 46.9 J kg−1 K−1, stated as the largest among known lanthanide-exclusive clusters. Propionate-, 1,2,3-cyclohexanetriol-, and chloroacetate-supported clusters are cited as having lower −ΔSM because heavier ligands and large anions lower magnetic density.
scope: Molecular coolants based on high-nuclearity, weakly anisotropic Gd(III)-exclusive hydroxide clusters, evaluated by isothermal magnetic entropy change.
conditions: Comparison at ΔH = 70 kOe; spin density expressed as unpaired electrons per gram.
caveats: The linear density trend is qualified in the same section by magnetic coupling. The Markdown assigns 41.8 and 43.6 J kg−1 K−1 inconsistently among Gd27, Gd48, and related clusters, so those secondary numbers should not be used without the original papers.
